transcript: The current production of A Streetcar Named Desire starring Paul Mescal at BAM is far more terrifying than you'd remember from your high school English class. At least, that was the case for me. In this moody, stark, and violent version directed by Rebecca Frecknall, no one is a caricature and everyone means exactly what they say, no matter how poetic. Blanche, astoundingly inhabited by Patsy Ferran, leaves the biggest impression in this production, and the chemistry she has with Stan and Stella heightens the psychological warfare that she endures. Paul Mescal exceeded my expectations, bringing a uniquely sinister and calculating element to Stan, that made him much scarier than I had envisioned. And Anjana Vasan who plays Stella is also fantastic, rendering her character complex and caring but ultimately unforgivable. The relatively simple blocking on a mostly bare, wooden square of a stage, around which everyone is a lurking witness, contributes to Blanche’s isolation and sense of confinement. There are some directorial choices that didn't land for me, but I found the core vision to be very effective and perfectly calibrated with the performances. The energy was palpable and chilling, and I was left equally in awe of the performances and disturbed by this American classic that I already knew the ending to. If you can, definitely see this production. I believe the run at BAM is sold out, but I'd be surprised if it doesn't transfer to Broadway. It is not to be missed. With that, another program for my collection.
